name: PavementSense
description: The proposed road-surface dataset was developed for automated road-surface condition assessment, road-damage classification, and computer vision applications for infrastructure monitoring. It contains three classes: Major Damage, Minor Damage, and Normal, representing different levels of road-surface conditions. The images were collected in Barishal district, Bangladesh, under natural road and weather conditions. They capture diverse surface textures, lighting conditions, viewpoints, and road surroundings. Each image was visually inspected and labeled according to the dominant road-surface condition. Major Damage includes severe potholes, significant cracks, deformation, and extensive surface loss. Minor Damage contains small holes, local cracks, surface imperfections, and minor deformations. Normal represents road surfaces without significant visible damage. The dataset contains 2,855 original images, comprising 1,907 Major Damage, 354 Minor Damage, and 594 Normal images. Before augmentation, the images were split into training, validation, and test sets in a 7:1:2 ratio, resulting in 1,996, 290, and 569 images, respectively. Splitting was performed before augmentation to prevent data leakage across subsets. To address class imbalance, 2,504 additional training images were generated using random rotation, brightness and contrast adjustment, Gaussian blurring, and hue and saturation shifts. These included 166 Major Damage, 1,253 Minor Damage, and 1,085 Normal images.
